title: Testing Module Functions
story: Your math module has a dozen functions. Before sharing it with your team, you need confidence it's correct. A systematic test suite per module catches regressions and documents expected behavior — turning 'it should work' into 'it DOES work.'
why: Module-level tests verify that functions work correctly in isolation and together, creating a safety net for future changes.
analogy: Before a bridge opens, engineers test every beam, bolt, and cable individually, then test the whole structure under load. Module tests are your bridge inspection: test each function alone (unit), then test them working together (integration).
try_it: Add `area_circle(radius: Float64)` and `circumference(radius: Float64)` to geometry. Write tests using approximate comparison (tolerance of 0.01). Add tests for edge cases: zero dimensions, negative dimensions (should these be errors?).
tips: One test function per logical group (e.g., test_math, test_string)
Test zero inputs, negative inputs, and maximum values — edge cases find bugs
Use .unwrap() for Option results you know should succeed, or check .is_none()
common_mistakes: Not testing enough different inputs — a single test case proves nothing
Forgetting to test error paths — what happens with division by zero?
Writing tests that depend on each other — each test should be independent
